page: Microsoft Azure E160as_v7 is an Easv7-series virtual machine configured with 160 dedicated vCPUs and 1280.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 80 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration provides a high density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, positioning the instance within the memory-optimized category. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and SHA_NI, which accelerate cryptographic and vector calculations.

Benchmark evaluations place the E160as_v7 in the top tier across multiple performance dimensions. The system demonstrates exceptional processing capability, as evidenced by top-tier scores in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as PassMark CPU and memory evaluations. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 462.89 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 209.83 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database and transactional performance are also notable, with Redis SET operations reaching 196.39 million operations per second and static web serving throughput peaking at 120.22 GB/sec.

While the instance delivers top-tier CPU and memory performance, it lacks local storage and GPU hardware, meaning workloads requiring local NVMe scratch space or hardware-accelerated parallel processing must rely on external Premium Storage. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and massive memory capacity provides a highly consolidated platform for resource-intensive enterprise workloads. The E160as_v7 is optimized for large-scale databases, memory-intensive analytics, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks where high memory capacity and fast memory bandwidth are critical.
